pairs.why: A's saddle sits properly over the top fence rail with its strap and stirrup hanging naturally, while B's saddle seems pasted in front of the rail and its horn is an odd tube.
B's keypad has labelled digits and operators like a working calculator, while A's keys are blank and could not be used.
A's wall clock hangs flat against the wall like the real card, while B's round clock stands on its rim on the floor with nothing to stop it rolling.
A's X-legs, armrests and seat frame all join at clear pivots, while in B the front seat bar sticks out past the frame and the back posts don't clearly meet the leg cross.
In A one clamp holds the yoke cleanly to the truss with side pivots, while B adds a decorative band and its truss end has a loose stub.
A's armrests sit on posts that run down into the legs, while B's armrests and padded seat rim look tacked on, with the arm supports barely reaching the X-frame.
B's yoke hangs from two clamps on the truss with clear pivot knobs, while A's single clamp and hidden left pivot leave the attachment less clear.
A's clock hangs flat on the wall, while B's round clock balances on its rim on the floor with no stand.
